question: Will anyone besides Gianni Infantino have publicly declared a candidacy for the 2027 FIFA presidency as of October 15, 2026?

calls.reasoning: As of Sep 29-Oct 5 2026, Infantino remains the only declared candidate; Montagliani is 'considering/exploring', UEFA says it will present a challenger before the Nov 18 nomination deadline. Only ~10 days remain in the window, which closes ~5 weeks before the nomination deadline; in past contested cycles (2015-16) most challengers declared in the final weeks before the deadline (Salman and Infantino on deadline day). Montagliani and Ceferin are currently negotiating funding concessions with FIFA, suggesting leverage play rather than imminent declaration. Upside: UEFA could name a candidate early to build momentum, or a fringe figure could declare (fringe declarations happened in 2015). No human market matches this contract: the Polymarket 'Infantino out by Dec 31' (0.09) and Manifold markets are about him leaving office, not about challenger declarations by Oct 15.
calls.dossier:
- Wikipedia '77th FIFA Congress' (accessed 2026-10-05): Infantino declared 30 Apr 2026 at Vancouver Congress; only declared candidate; Victor Montagliani listed as 'exploring', 'reportedly preparing to announce'. Nomination deadline 18 Nov 2026 23:59 CET, 5 member-association endorsements needed.
- Al Jazeera 2026-09-29: no candidate had officially declared against Infantino; seven weeks remained. Montagliani and UEFA's Ceferin jointly wrote to FIFA seeking payments to member associations; Infantino open to 'additional funding' (read as courting votes).
- Search snippets (ESPN, late Sep 2026): Montagliani seen as most likely challenger, would have UEFA/AFC/CONCACAF backing, yet to declare; Infantino sent letter to 211 members about 'reforms' ~Sep 29.
- Canadian Soccer Daily 2026-08-01/08-14 (Reuters, TalkSport): Montagliani weighing whether to challenge now or wait until the post is vacant; has made no public commitment.
- Ceferin ruled himself out (podcast); Al-Khelaifi ruled himself out. UEFA has said it intends to present a rival candidate before the November deadline.
- Blatter reportedly backed Lise Klaveness (Norway FA) as a successor; no declaration by her found. Salman (AFC) and Mattias Grafstrom have been mentioned; no declarations found.
- Inside World Football 2026-09-29: FIFA accused UEFA of 'harassment' of Infantino (article blocked, headline only). France, England, Wales, Italy, Switzerland FAs have withdrawn support; UAFA (Arab federations) backs Infantino.
- Historical timing: in the 2015-16 cycle (deadline 26 Oct 2015) Prince Ali declared ~Sep 9, Champagne in Oct, Salman and Infantino on/near deadline day; minor figures (Nakhid, Bility, others) also declared publicly. In the 2011 cycle bin Hammam declared in March for a June vote. Challengers often declare in the final weeks before the nomination deadline.
- Status quo: Infantino is the sole declared candidate.
- Resolution: resolves on a public, unambiguous self-declaration (or an official statement from a football body the person leads) reported by credible media, not on FIFA's official candidate list; 'considering' or 'expected to' does not count.
- Event window: now -> 2026-10-15 23:59 UTC per the criteria (a cumulative state check at that moment); as of 2026-10-05 13:40 UTC about 10.4 days remain; the window ends ~34 days before the nomination deadline.
- Searched, not found: any declaration by any challenger as of early Oct 2026; any announced date for a Montagliani or UEFA decision; any fringe declarant; any human market on challenger declarations (only 'Infantino out' markets exist on Polymarket/Manifold, which have different terms).

Montagliani, the frontrunner, has hesitated for 8+ weeks: CONCACAF is divided (Caribbean nations back Infantino) and he faces his own CONCACAF re-election in Feb 2027. Historical FIFA challengers tended to declare near the nomination deadline (Infantino and Sheikh Salman on deadline day in Oct 2015), and this year's deadline is Nov 18, a month after the window closes. Upside: a European confederations meeting in Berlin on Oct 8, ESPN sources hinting at developments after the Copenhagen clubs' assembly, and the chance that a fringe candidate declares. No matching human market was found; Polymarket and Manifold only price Infantino leaving office (~9-11%), which is a different contract.

Infantino's support is consolidating (UAFA endorsement Oct 2; all confederations except UEFA reportedly behind him), which raises the cost of a challenge. Only ~10 days remain while the nomination deadline is Nov 18; historically serious FIFA challengers (2015-16 cycle) often declared close to the deadline, and the FIFA Council's Oct 15 governance-review meeting gives potential challengers a reason to wait. Upside: UEFA is actively recruiting, ECA/UEFA rhetoric is escalating, and a fringe declarant reported by credible media would count. No matching human market exists; Polymarket's 'Infantino out by Dec 31' (0.09, $513k) and Manifold's 'announces out before end of 2026' (0.11) are near-misses about him leaving office, not about a challenger declaring, so they are evidence only.

calls.reasoning: As of the latest reports (Sep 29 to Oct 5, 2026), Infantino is still the only declared candidate. Montagliani, the likeliest challenger, has been 'exploring' for 8+ weeks while CONCACAF is split and his own CONCACAF re-election is due in Feb 2027. Only about 10 days remain, and the window closes roughly 5 weeks before the Nov 18 nomination deadline. In the 2015-16 cycle, serious challengers often declared close to the deadline. Infantino's support outside UEFA is consolidating, and the FIFA Council's Oct 15 governance meeting gives challengers a reason to wait. Upside: UEFA says it will field a challenger before the deadline, there is a European confederations meeting in Berlin on Oct 8, ESPN reported 'developments' might follow, and a fringe declarant would also count. No human market matches this contract; the 'Infantino out' markets (Polymarket 0.09, Manifold 0.11) are near-misses.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: no challenger as of early October 2026, Montagliani only exploring, Čeferin, Al-Khelaifi and Motsepe out, nomination deadline Nov 18, and no matching market. The differences are additive, not contradictory. Run 2 adds the Oct 8 Berlin meeting of European confederations and the Feb 2027 CONCACAF re-election. Run 3 adds the Oct 15 FIFA Council meeting and the UAFA endorsement. Neither was checked on this run because no web access was available. I accept them as plausible, and they roughly offset each other: Berlin is a catalyst for an earlier declaration, while the Council meeting and Infantino's consolidating support are reasons to delay. What remains is a judgment call: how likely a declaration is in 10 days, given months of hesitation and history that points to declarations near the deadline. I would bet slightly below 0.2.
